questions.question_text:
A wildlife app uses this pictograph.
How many bilbies were recorded?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]
\node at (3.5,3.4) {Night survey}; \node[right] at (0,2.3) {Bilbies}; \node[right] at (0,1.4) {Bandicoots}; \foreach \x in {2.5,3.2,3.9,4.6,5.3,6.0} {\fill (\x,2.3) circle (4pt);} \foreach \x in {2.5,3.2,3.9,4.6} {\fill (\x,1.4) circle (4pt);} \fill (2.5,0.3) circle (4pt); \node[right] at (2.8,0.3) {$=5$ animals};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Counts the bilby symbols but does not multiply by the key value of five.
Uses four symbols from the bandicoot row and multiplies by six instead of reading the key.
Adds the six bilby symbols to the key value rather than multiplying.

questions.question_text:
The pictograph shows wildlife water stations refilled.
How many more stations were refilled in Ridge than Creek?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.9]
\node at (3.5,3.4) {Stations refilled}; \node[right] at (0,2.3) {Ridge}; \node[right] at (0,1.4) {Creek}; \foreach \x in {2.5,3.2,3.9,4.6,5.3,6.0,6.7} {\draw (\x,2.3) circle (5pt);} \foreach \x in {2.5,3.2,3.9,4.6} {\draw (\x,1.4) circle (5pt);} \draw (2.5,0.3) circle (5pt); \node[right] at (2.8,0.3) {$=3$ stations};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Finds the three-symbol difference but does not apply the key of three stations.
Adds all eleven symbols and multiplies by the key instead of finding a difference.
Gives Creek's total, $4\times3$, rather than the difference between rows.

questions.solution_text:
The rows differ by $7-4=3$ symbols.
$3\times3=9$
Ridge had $9$ more stations refilled.

questions.question_text:
A rescue blog shows $5$ bird symbols and $7$ reptile symbols.
Each symbol represents $4$ animals.
How many animals are shown altogether?

options.why: Adds the symbols but does not multiply the total by four animals per symbol.
Calculates only the reptile row, $7\times4$, and omits the bird row.
Multiplies the four-animal key by the difference between the two rows instead of their total.

questions.question_text:
A council webpage gives the table below.
How many more nesting boxes were installed at Coast than Valley?
$\begin{array}{c|r}\text{Area}&\text{Boxes}\\\hline\text{Coast}&46\\\text{Valley}&29\\\text{Ranges}&38\\\text{Plains}&33\end{array}$

options.why: Adds the Coast and Valley values instead of finding how many more.
Subtracts the Ranges value from Coast instead of using Valley.
Subtracts Plains from Coast instead of comparing Coast with Valley.

questions.question_text:
A post claims, ‘At least $70$ lizards counted.’ Its pictograph shows $8$ symbols and the key says one symbol represents $8$ lizards.
Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: The claim is false because the display shows $64$ lizards
The claim is true because the display shows $72$ lizards
options.why: Adds the eight symbols to the key value instead of multiplying them.

options.text: The claim is true because eight symbols is more than seven
options.why: Compares symbol counts without converting them to lizards or checking the threshold of seventy.

options.text: The claim is false because the display shows $16$ lizards
options.why: Adds the symbol count and key value instead of multiplying $8\times8$.

questions.question_text:
An infographic contains $12$ identical symbols for a reported total of $72$ wildlife checks.
Another row has $9$ symbols using the same key.
What does the second row represent?

options.why: Adds the inferred key of six to the reported total of seventy-two instead of multiplying nine symbols.
Multiplies the nine symbols by twelve symbols rather than by six checks per symbol.
Adds nine symbols to the inferred key value of six instead of multiplying.
